 Dated this the 2nd day of February 2016  JUDGMENT
The challenge in the writ petition is against Exts.P10 orders passed by the 1st respondent and P11 order passed by the 3rd respondent, under the Kerala Value Added Tax (KVAT) Act .

The brief facts that led to the filing of the writ petition are that, the petitioner, who is a dealer in energy drinks under the brand name 'Red Bull' had approached this Court earlier, through W.P.(C). 35373/2015,
aggrieved by the pre-assessment notices, that were served on him proposing the completion of an assessment, and imposition of a penalty under the KVAT Act, for the assessment year 2014-15.
The issue involved in the pre-assessment notices was basically with regard to classification of the products dealt with by the petitioner, for the purposes of taxation, under the KVAT Act.

The petitioner had also approached the 3rd respondent with an application for clarification and the same was pending consideration before the 3rd respondent at a time when the pre- assessment notices were issued to the petitioner.

On finding that an adjudication of the matter at the hand of the 1st respondent would be a futile exercise, especially when the application for clarification was pending before the 3rd respondent, this Court had disposed W.P.(C) No.35373/2015, by directing the authority for clarification, to consider and pass orders on the clarification petition, within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment, after hearing the petitioner, and also directing that further proceedings pursuant to the pre-assessment notices served on the petitioner be kept in abeyance, till such time as the authority for clarification passed orders in the clarification petition as directed, and communicated the same, to the petitioner.

It would appear that by two orders (produced together as Ext.P10 in the writ petition), both dated 18.11.2015, that were served on the petitioner on 23.11.2015, the date of Ext.P9 judgment, the 1st respondent had completed the assessment proceedings pursuant to the pre-assessment notices that were impugned in the earlier writ petition. Taking note of the said orders passed by the 1st respondent, the 3rd respondent, to whom the matter with regard to passing orders on the clarification application was delegated by the 2nd respondent, passed Ext.P11 order, holding that the application for clarification could not be considered, since the 1st respondent had already passed an adjudication order in the matter.

In the writ petition, Exts.P10 orders of the 1st respondent and P11 order of the 3rd respondent are impugned inter alia on the ground that Ext.P10 orders were passed to over reach the directions in Ext.P9 judgment, and Ext.P11 order, while erroneous in the reasoning contained therein, also suffers from the defect of having been passed by an authority different from the one to whom the directions in Ext.P9 judgment were \addressed.
2. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader for the respondents.

sentences.text: On a consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions made across the Bar, I am of the view that, since the intention of this Court while passing Ext.P9 judgment was to ensure that an adjudication would follow the order passed by the authority for clarification under the KVAT Act, and the said object has not been materialised through the passing of Exts.P10 orders by the 1st respondent and P11 order by the authority for clarification, Ext.P10 orders should be quashed and the 3rd respondent has to be directed to pass orders on merits in the application for clarification preferred by the petitioner.

I, therefore, quash Exts.P10 orders passed by the 1st respondent and direct the 3rd respondent to pass fresh orders on the application for clarification submitted by the petitioner, after affording the petitioner an opportunity of hearing.
The 3rd respondent shall pass fresh orders as directed, within a period of one month, from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, after hearing the petitioner.

The 1st respondent shall pass fresh orders of assessment in relation to the petitioner, only after the 3rd respondent authority for clarification has passed an order as directed in this judgment and after hearing the petitioner,
subsequent to the orders passed by the 3rd respondent.
The writ petition is disposed as above.

opennyai_summary.decision:
On a consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions made across the Bar, I am of the view that, since the intention of this Court while passing Ext.P9 judgment was to ensure that an adjudication would follow the order passed by the authority for clarification under the KVAT Act, and the said object has not been materialised through the passing of Exts.P10 orders by the 1st respondent and P11 order by the authority for clarification, Ext.P10 orders should be quashed and the 3rd respondent has to be directed to pass orders on merits in the application for clarification preferred by the petitioner.
I, therefore, quash Exts.P10 orders passed by the 1st respondent and direct the 3rd respondent to pass fresh orders on the application for clarification submitted by the petitioner, after affording the petitioner an opportunity of hearing.
The 3rd respondent shall pass fresh orders as directed, within a period of one month, from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, after hearing the petitioner.
The 1st respondent shall pass fresh orders of assessment in relation to the petitioner, only after the 3rd respondent authority for clarification has passed an order as directed in this judgment and after hearing the petitioner,
subsequent to the orders passed by the 3rd respondent.
The writ petition is disposed as above.
